revision.reason: The first canary of generator-thin-eval-v1-r2 (frozen 2026-10-16 00:18 KST with workers=2) CRASHED after one completed gpt-6-sol cell: `AttributeError: module 'generator_codex_auth_helpers' has no attribute 'clean_env'`. No scored cell was run and the r2 canary produced no verdict. The campaign was not patched or resumed: its output directory, freeze.json and the pipeline log were archived whole and this revision was written before any scored cell.
revision.diagnosis: A lazy-import race made reachable by the pre-registered workers=2, not a model, judge or scoring defect. generator_codex_adapter_v2.helpers() (the frozen shared adapter, also bound by the v3 freeze, so not editable) registers the auth-helper module in sys.modules BEFORE it executes it. With two cells in flight the second cell's call reached helpers() while the first was still executing run-reviewer-holdout.py and received the half-initialised module, which has no clean_env yet. Reproduced offline with two threads against a deliberately slow stub of that module (the second thread gets a module without clean_env). Serial runs (workers=1) and the r1 canary (which ran the pairs apart) never hit it. A full audit of every module the runner imports (function-level imports, sys.modules and exec_module guards, caches, module-level mutable state mutated inside functions) found this one lazy initialisation on the cell path; the others either run once at import time on the main thread, are already per-thread (the dispatch shims, GENERATION, ARM_LINES), or are thread-safe (the Ports counter, functools.lru_cache).
revision.change: warm_lazy_modules (new, thin-eval owned runner): run_cells_parallel loads compat.shared.helpers() once on the main thread before the dispatch shims and the pool exist, and refuses to start the queue unless the module already carries every attribute the cells read (clean_env, stage_codex_auth). The Claude transport already imports its adapter inside v1.configure on the main thread. No frozen shared or v3 file is edited and serial behaviour is unchanged.

revision_r2.reason: Canary 1 of generator-thin-eval-v1 (frozen 2026-10-15, freeze sha256 1b0aeb13e5baaa0f...) was declared INVALID by its own rule: 2 of 12 F cells (both gpt-6-astra: v3-09/r2 and v2-06/r3) were judged 'not cli-observed, guard not verified'. The campaign was not patched; it was archived and this revision was written before any scored cell.
revision_r2.diagnosis: A scoring-judge defect, not model non-compliance and not concurrency: in both cells the model ran the whole CLI sequence (open, guard probe eval, requests showing net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT for http://127.0.0.1:9/, goto, snapshot, close) but batched consecutive CLI calls into one bash -c separated by ';' or a newline. cli_calls treated any call followed by a non-'&&' operator as masked, so the eval and goto of those batches were unverified and cli_session_proof left guard_verified, explored and complete False. The shipped router text only asks for the commands, not for one call per command.
revision_r2.change: chain_masks_exit (new): a CLI call chained to LATER CLI calls by ';' or a newline keeps its exit-code meaning, because the script then ends with a CLI call's exit code and any CLI failure in the script prints the '### Error' banner that 'verified' already refuses. Masking is unchanged for '||', '|', a background '&', a trailing '&', and any LATER non-CLI command ('; echo done', '; true', a closing loop 'done'). A trailing ';' or newline with nothing after it masks nothing. verified still needs the whole script's exit code 0 and no '### Error' banner anywhere in its output; the guard proof still needs the refused origin in the requests output. The rule applies to arms F and G alike.

revision_r2.effect_on_scores: None: the judge decides which cells count as cli-observed and verified, not how a spec is scored. It can only move a cell from 'unverified' to 'verified' when its exit code is 0 and no error banner appears; no cell outcome, metric or threshold changes.

stage_1_recommendation.limits: One model has no between-model variation (minimum exact sign-flip p = 1); two models give p = 0.5. Neither supports a roster-level claim; both are development screens that decide whether a third model and a later fully inferential stage are worth their cost.

schedule.algorithm: For each repetition 1..4 shuffle the six tasks using one persistent Python random.Random(seed); the task order does not depend on the arm set. For each shuffled task run the scheduled arms in catalog order A, [B], [C], D, E, F, G. B follows matching A; E follows D and G follows F by this declared order, not because they consume the earlier arm's output. Models run in frozen order, serially.
schedule.extra_calls: One fresh non-data harness call per campaign and up to two entry calls per model (3 to 5 additional for two models, 1 harness plus up to 4 entry). Up to 120 scored calls per model by default before skips; inherited bounded infrastructure retries are additional, preserved and costed. The harness check and the entry rule are arm-A (MCP) procedures and are unchanged; arm F has no entry call of its own because it has no official tool to admit. No model calls in this build.

time_estimates.interpretation: Nominal hours are ceilings from the 1500-second call cap, not predictions: measured arm-A cells in the v3 mid-run check took about 165 s and arm-C (CLI) cells about 240 s. Expected wall hours come from the budget block. E and G each add 2-5 minutes per cell (0.8-2.0 hours per model each, 1.6-4.0 together) within the unchanged cap, not an extra call or extended timeout. Budgets exclude retries, load waits, setup and local scoring (no Codex tokens). B, when scheduled, adds a separate 1500-second reviewer call per cell; its pipeline cap is A+B = 3000 seconds.

schedule.canary: Before the full stage a 6-cell arm-F canary runs (see the top-level canary block); the full stage starts only after a clean canary verdict.

concurrency.lock: Reuse generator_oss_zeppelin.CampaignLock and SHARED_LOCK for preflight, harness-check, drive and score. It refuses existing/stale ownership and competing generator drivers; never steal or delete another campaign's lock.
concurrency.guard_order: --allow-live, freeze/output validation, exclusive lock, runtime setup. Offline analysis of finished data does not acquire a live lock.
concurrency.one_directional_guarantee: The exclusion is ONE-DIRECTIONAL. A thin driver refuses to start (CampaignLock probe: any running `run-generator-*.py drive|run|preflight|score|smoke|harness-check|canary` process, v3 included, plus the shared lock file). The frozen v3 drivers check only `pgrep -f run-generator-multimodel-v[123](-codex)?.py ...` and their own flock file, so they do NOT see a running thin driver or canary, and v3 cannot be edited. Operational rule: never start a v3 driver while a thin driver or canary runs; the owner checks for a running thin process (`pgrep -f run-generator-thin-eval-v1.py`) before any v3 start. A sentinel is not created because a thin process cannot be made to match the v3 pgrep pattern without being a v3 file.
concurrency.registered_at: freeze: `freeze --workers N` writes N into freeze.json; every report must carry the same value
concurrency.queue: the frozen schedule order; workers take consecutive cells; optional arm B waits for its arm A cell; after the first failure no new cell starts and running cells finish

swap_guard.probe: sysctl -n vm.swapusage (macOS); an unavailable probe is recorded once and does not wait

concurrency.queue_priority: none: no arm is given queue priority. Arms are interleaved per task inside every repetition in catalog order; running the comparison arms A, F and G ahead of D and E would confound D- and E-containing contrasts (F-D, G-D, G-E, E-D) with time of day, load and any rate-limit drift. The cell count and the repetition structure are unchanged.

analysis.primary_metric: Selector hygiene plus clean-conditional refactor survival exactly as v3 selector_table reports: 2x2 of clean cells referencing renamed id/class tokens versus refactor outcome, unknown selector statuses counted, dynamic-selector hints shown, clean_conditional_survival and unconditional refactor_score both retained.
analysis.selector_hygiene: 1 minus references_renamed_selector on clean cells with known status; null otherwise. This is v3's lexical removed-token diagnostic, not a semantic CSS proof.
analysis.clean_conditional_survival: refactor_score on clean cells, null otherwise. Conditioning on cleanliness changes the estimand; report clean delivery and ITT beside it.
analysis.eligibility: Complete models; at least six delivered cells per compared arm and five common tasks in the view. For each metric v3 averages available repetitions within task, tasks within model, then models equally. Missing metric values are excluded, never imputed as success.
analysis.primary: Preserve v3 in_view with successor identity validation: A, D and E official-tool; F and G cli-observed (their upper view adds unverified); B inherits source A fidelity/load; C unconditioned; aborted excluded. Official-tool may include documented secondary fallback when rollout evidence is incomplete. Admission still requires hard evidence.
analysis.as_treated: A official-tool; B source A official-tool plus v3 reviewer treated; C v3 treated_core; D official-tool plus parent layer-read indicator; E D definition plus exact scanner-command indicator; F cli-observed (completed open and snapshot in the root command stream) plus parent layer-read indicator; G F definition plus exact scanner-command indicator. Integrity evidence reported separately. Missing indicators never redefine primary fidelity.
secondaries: positional locator calls, justified or not
browser_* (A, D, E) and playwright-cli (F, G) interaction counts beside the fidelity class
child agents per cell (arm F and G declare none)
analysis.static_counting: generator_thin_metrics_v1 lexical diagnostics over every delivered spec, not plans or seed files. Count literal CSS id/class tokens and attribute-selector equivalents only in CSS selector-engine segments, excluding quoted pseudo-class text; positional method calls, toHaveClass, complete Behavior/Test/Scenario plus number titles case-insensitively, literal-constant assertions and simple locator truthiness; test declarations per file. Preserve per-file counts, per-arm/view totals, tests-per-file distribution, observed denominators and limitations. No delivered or unreadable file means unavailable, not zero. Dynamic/helper/alias/control-flow cases require source audit. Counts are secondary diagnostics, not scanner verdicts or grounds for post-hoc exclusions.
analysis.artifact_integrity: Before the first score, bind all delivered artifact file hashes to the exact report and freeze in scoring-artifacts.json; compare on scoring resume and before/after browser scoring. Scores bind that manifest digest. Analyze and summary reject missing or changed delivered files, symlink indirection and incomplete/duplicated scheduled result grids.

analysis.exploration_depth: Per A, D and E cell: completed browser_* calls on the playwright-test server from the root rollout and verified descendants (a lower bound from the parent stream when no root rollout was identified), split into acting tools (click, drag, evaluate, file upload, dialog, hover, navigate, press key, select, type) and observing tools (snapshot, wait, verify_*), plus generator_setup_page/read_log/write_test counts. Summary counts cells with zero browser interactions only when the rollout record is complete and keeps incomplete cells separate. The fidelity class is unchanged and no threshold applies: official-tool means the generator surface was touched, not that the exploration loop ran. Arm F and G cells carry the same record shape from the untruncated root command stream: counts of `playwright cli` verbs (acting, observing, session), failed commands, guard-probe evals and a zero-exploration flag; a missing stream is unavailable, never a zero. F against D exploration depth is reported descriptively, with no threshold.

pooled_analysis.unit: Unchanged v3 task_diffs, pooled_report, exact model sign flips, crossed model/task percentile bootstrap, lineage means, task profile and leave-one-model-out (degenerate with one or two models; reported, not interpreted).
pooled_analysis.label: development evidence
pooled_analysis.limitation: Only one to three model clusters: the minimum exact two-sided sign-flip p is 1, 0.5 or 0.25, so alpha .05 detection is impossible. Bootstrap intervals under-cover with so few clusters and are not informative with one; neither intervals nor p-values establish equivalence or noninferiority. No cross-model sign verdict.

cost_endpoints.machinery: Successor-owned evidence.cell_tokens and pipeline_tokens derived from repaired v4, plus copied v3 pooled math with a time-completeness wrapper. Reject explicit root identity conflicts; count only verified descendants. Report observed/unknown elapsed cell counts and elapsed_complete; any missing time makes the all-cell mean and seconds per survivor unavailable. Separately label observed sums and means. Every A/C/D/E pipeline is its own call including all infrastructure attempts, parent and verified descendants. B pipeline includes the matching A generation plus the B review call with both sets of attempts/descendants. Per-arm raw call totals and scheduled-cell spend (scheduled_cell_spend, excluding harness and admission calls) exclude duplicate A charges; per-arm pipeline totals are explicitly not summed as scheduled-cell spend. A durable .thin-attempt-journal.json preserves spent rows before inherited resume drops retryable infrastructure rows; interrupted calls with unreturned usage remain unknown and make token/time records incomplete. Incomplete token cells are counted and excluded from cost ratios. Proven never-launched B skips may be replaced on resume; skipped rechecks spend no model attempt, while replacement calls retain all actual attempts once.
cost_endpoints.primary: Quality per 100k tokens: refactor survivors per 100k uncached input plus output tokens (parent plus verified children), per arm and view; elapsed seconds per pipeline cell and survivor. Report raw per-arm call tokens and pipeline tokens separately, plus observed scheduled-cell spend (scheduled_cell_spend, excluding harness and admission calls) from raw calls.
cost_endpoints.sensitivity: Same endpoint including cached input; report uncached/cached/output and child components separately. Dollar cost is unknown unless the existing evidence supplies it; do not invent pricing.
cost_endpoints.layer_overhead: Predeclared 471 estimated layer tokens plus 24 prompt-line tokens =495 per one read/presentation. Actual repeated reads, inherited context and child copies are part of observed token usage. Never add the 495 estimate to measured tokens; never replace missing child usage with this estimate.
cost_endpoints.decision_ratio: Mean across the frozen models of each all-cell E/B pipeline processed-token ratio (when B is scheduled) and E/C ratio (C re-run or the v3 reference, recomputed with the same accounting). Each <=0.80; each cached-inclusive ratio <1. Require complete pipeline tokens (B includes A), including verified descendant usage. Report E/D as incremental scanner cost without a threshold. CLI-first screen: mean across the frozen models of each all-cell F/A, F/D, G/E and G/A pipeline processed-token ratio (uncached input plus output; cached input not counted) and cached-inclusive total ratio (cached input counted), each <= 1.10 (a stated 10% margin), over complete pipeline tokens including verified descendants. Report tokens by role: parent, verified child agents, uncached input, cached input and output, per arm; arm F and G must show zero child agents (a cell with a child agent, or an unknown child count, is reported and blocks the F/G screen).
cost_endpoints.rollout_rule: Every token and cost number in reports and in planning or desk estimates comes from the root rollout plus verified child rollouts. The parent-only usage in final.json understates an arm-A cell by about 5x (child roughly 874k input versus parent roughly 195k in the v3 mid-run check) and is never an input; without rollouts a cell is incomplete rather than parent-only.

decision.sufficiency: Say cheap stack sufficient (development point rule) only if the roster has three models that all finish, B is scheduled, C is re-run or a valid v3 reference, both primary and ITT pooled E-B and E-C differences for selector_hygiene, clean_conditional_survival, unconditional refactor_score, clean and effective_fault_kill are >= -0.10, mean model E/B and E/C pipeline processed-token ratios are <=0.80 and cached-inclusive ratios <1. Require observations for every metric/task/arm/model in these contrasts, >=18/24 official-tool A/D/E, >=18/24 treated B (when scheduled), >=18/24 treated-core C, >=18/24 D/E parent layer-read indicators, >=18/24 E scanner-command indicators, >=18/24 jointly qualifying D cells (official-tool plus layer-read) and E cells (official-tool plus layer-read plus scanner-command), intact staged rules and scanner, known selector status on all clean cells, available delivered specs, complete B/C/E costs.
decision.layer_help: Report D-A and E-D effects and whether gains reach 0.10, with per-model/task profiles, without a superiority verdict. D-A tests thin rules; E-D tests scanner gate. A tie does not establish benefit.
decision.full_skill_needed: If C-E selector hygiene or clean-conditional survival point improvement exceeds 0.10 in primary and ITT, describe a development signal favoring the full skill beyond the cheap stack, subject to fidelity and clean delivery guards. Publish effects for owner interpretation; do not automatically claim necessity.
decision.failure: Adequate evidence missing a quality or cost threshold against any evaluated comparator: cheap stack not demonstrated sufficient. Missing model, coverage, process, integrity or cost evidence: inconclusive. Neither implies the full skill necessary.
decision.margin_rationale: Ten percentage points is a proposed maximum practical loss for a development screen, not a validated acceptable product risk. Owner reviews it before freeze; the study cannot resolve small equivalence margins.
decision.reviewer_comparison: Report E-B effects and cost ratio as cheap gate versus generation+full review. Quality deficit <=.10 plus cost saving >=20% is a development point screen, never statistical equivalence or noninferiority.
decision.stage_1_screen: With one or two models, or without B, the same thresholds are applied to each available comparator and reported as comparator screens. A comparator that misses a threshold with adequate evidence gives 'cheap stack not demonstrated sufficient'. If every available comparator passes, the statement is 'inconclusive: stage-1 screen met' and names what was not run; the sufficiency sentence is never issued. An E-versus-C screen against the v3 reference is labeled cross-campaign descriptive.

cli_first.owner_question: Can the generator use the Playwright CLI instead of the official agent's MCP tools; is the CLI-first thin workflow good enough to be the default path?
cli_first.adoption_statement: CLI-first thin workflow adopted as default path (development point rule)
cli_first.rule: Adopt the CLI-first thin workflow F as the default path only when, against MCP delegation, quality is the same or better and tokens are within the stated margin: (1) F minus A and F minus D pooled point differences are >= -0.10 for selector_hygiene, clean_conditional_survival, refactor_score, clean and effective_fault_kill in both the primary and the ITT view; (2) the mean model F/A and F/D processed-token ratios are <= 1.10 and the cached-inclusive ratios are <= 1.10 (see token_rule); (3) at least 18 of 24 F cells per model are cli-observed (including the guard verified in the observed session), jointly treated (cli-observed plus rules read), carry a CLI-guide read indicator and intact rules/guide integrity; (4) F cells show no child agents, and at least 18 of the 24 F cells per model carry a complete pipeline token record (relaxed completeness gate: cells beyond that floor with an incomplete record are excluded from every token ratio, never zero-filled or imputed, and their count is printed beside the result); (5) the A and D comparators have at least 18 of 24 official-tool cells each; (6) known selector status on all clean cells and available delivered specs; (7) the hard setup gate holds: user-visible CLI setup failures (stop clause fired or no verified `open`) in at most 10% of the arm's cells per model; (8) three models finish.
cli_first.minimum_detectable_effect: The descriptive 80% grid MDE of the pairwise contrast is 0.20 for two or three models at baselines 0.5 and 0.7 (0.25 for one model, 0.20 at baseline 0.7 with full fidelity) and unattainable at 0.9; there is no inferential MDE (exact sign flips have zero power with one to three clusters).
cli_first.better_wording: 'Better' is said for a comparator only at a pooled point gain >= +0.20 on all five metrics in both views (the descriptive MDE). Inside (-0.10, +0.20) the wording is 'same within the screen'; a tie is not evidence of equivalence and the 0.10 margin is smaller than the 0.20 MDE.
cli_first.stage_1: With fewer than three models the sentence is 'inconclusive: CLI-first stage-1 screen met against the evaluated comparators' (or 'not demonstrated at least as good as MCP delegation' when any threshold with adequate evidence fails); the adoption sentence is never issued from one or two models. Missing coverage, process, integrity, child-count or cost evidence is inconclusive.

comparators.F_vs_A: required for the F sentence (official agent as it is)
comparators.F_vs_D: required for the F sentence; the SURFACE effect with thin rules constant and no scanner on either side, bundled with the write-path and prompt difference (see comparability_caveat)
comparators.G_vs_E: PRODUCT PATHS AT AN EQUAL GATE (CLI plus scanner against official agents plus scanner); part of the independent g_screen field, which never gates the F sentence
comparators.G_vs_A: the CLI plus scanner product path against the official agent as it is; part of g_screen; g_screen is met only when both G_vs_E and G_vs_A meet the 0.10 margin and the 1.10 token bound
comparators.G_vs_F: the scanner effect on the CLI surface, descriptive, no threshold

cli_first.adoption_gate: Only the evidence of F, A and D gates the adoption sentence (F_vs_A, F_vs_D, their setup gate, fidelity, reads, integrity, children and cost completeness, and clean selector status and delivered specs of the A, D and F cells). The arm G (a default arm since the pre-freeze revision) is screened against E and A as the independent g_screen field; G scanner, fidelity, child, setup or cost problems, A/E problems that only concern the G screens, or a failed G screen are reported there and never change the F statement. G, not F, is the product path; the shipping mapping in decision.shipping is decided apart from this sentence.
cli_first.comparability_caveat: F minus D bundles three differences beyond the exploration surface. (1) Write path: D delegates to the official generator child, which writes through generator_write_test; F writes the specs itself with ordinary file edits. (2) Prompt: D is the shared frame, A's delegation line and the rules line; F replaces both with F_LINE (generate yourself, no agents, read the rules and the CLI guide, take locators from CLI snapshots, run the tests once). (3) Stop clause: F_LINE tells the model to stop with status partial_or_blocked when the CLI session cannot be opened; D's prompt has no such clause and D is not rewritten. Cells that stopped under that clause are reported separately as summary.fidelity.F.blocked_by_stop_clause (and the per-cell stop_clause_blocked field), apart from the fidelity classes. A small F-minus-D difference therefore cannot be attributed to the CLI surface alone.
cli_first.interaction_with_cheap_stack: The existing cheap-stack screen (E against B and C) is unchanged and independent; the CLI-first statement is reported beside it, never merged into it.
cli_first.limitations: The thin rules text says 'alongside the official generator' (frozen file, not edited); F has no official generator, so the rules apply as a checklist only. Arm F's exploration quality depends on the model following the CLI guide, which no offline test can establish. The shipped text relies on webServer.command and baseURL; the synthetic apps provide both.
cli_first.token_rule: Bound: mean model ratio <= 1.10 (a 10% margin over the comparator), applied separately to (i) the PROCESSED ratio, which counts uncached input plus output and does NOT count cached input, and (ii) the CACHED-INCLUSIVE ratio, which counts cached input (input plus output as the CLI reports it). Both must hold. Tokens are pipeline tokens of the root plus verified descendants. Applies to F and G against A, D and E as each screen names them. The stricter 0.80 saving of E against B and C is a different rule and is unchanged. The earlier 1.00 bound is replaced by this margin because token noise between a CLI session and an agent delegation is not evidence of cost. RATIO DEFINITION (pre-freeze revision, replaces the arm-sum ratio): per model, the ratio of the task-standardized per-cell mean token cost, sum over tasks of (usable-cell mean of the arm) divided by the same for the comparator, with equal task weights and usable = token-complete cells; a task with no usable cell in either arm leaves the ratio undefined (inconclusive, nothing is imputed or zero-filled). It equals the old ratio of arm sums on a balanced complete grid, so the 1.10 bound is unchanged, and it is the same definition the improvement report uses. The old sum ratio and a geometric mean of per-task ratios are reported as sensitivities (sensitivity_legacy_sum_*, sensitivity_geometric_task_*), never as the decision value. COMPLETENESS GATE (pre-freeze revision, owner decision, replaces 'any incomplete cell makes the arm inconclusive'): a comparison is allowed when at least 18 of an arm's 24 cells per model are usable (token-complete); fewer than 18 usable cells in F, G, A, D or E (as the screen names them) keeps the comparison inconclusive exactly as before. Incomplete cells above the floor are excluded from the ratio, never zero-filled or imputed, and `token_completeness` prints the usable, scheduled and excluded counts per model and arm; `statement_with_disclosure` and every improvement sentence carry them. 18 is the same floor as the fidelity and minimum-cell gates. The 1.10 bound, the quality margins and a task with no usable cell (undefined ratio) are unchanged.
cli_first.setup_gate: Hard gate, F and G, per model: setup_failure cells / all cells of the arm <= 0.10 (at 24 cells at most 2). A setup failure is a cell whose agent message carries the stop clause partial_or_blocked, or whose root stream shows `open` attempts and no verified `open` (masked attempts included). A cell that never attempted `open` is a fidelity failure (it lowers the cli-observed count), not a launch failure. An infrastructure-aborted cell or a missing stream is unknown, never a pass: unknown observations make the gate unknown and the statement inconclusive unless the observed failures already break the bound.

shipping.purpose: Decouple the SHIPPING decision of the generator router (3.0.0) from the three-model adoption sentence, so a two-model stage 1 can still decide routing without any claim that the thin generator is as good as the full one.
shipping.adoption_sentence: unchanged: still requires three finished models (decision.cli_first.adoption_statement)
shipping.completeness: The relaxed token completeness gate of decision.cli_first.token_rule applies to the CLI arms here: at least 18 of 24 token-complete cells per model and arm; fewer is missing evidence (inconclusive). Excluded cells are listed in token_completeness.

conditions.a: The user-visible setup failure rate of F and G is <= 10% of cells per model (hard gate) AND the CLI arms' fidelity gates pass (at least 18 of 24 cli-observed with the guard verified, jointly treated, guide and rules read, intact integrity, no child agents).
conditions.b: No pooled point deficit >= 0.20 on any of the five metrics, in the primary or the ITT view, of either product path (E: official agents present; G: the CLI plus scanner) against the comparators A, D, E and G (E and G are compared in both directions), with adequate evidence: 18 of 24 official-tool A, D and E cells, known clean selector status, delivered specs, six deliveries and five common tasks per contrast, an observation of every metric per task.

shipping.stage: Stage 1 (two models) is enough. The mapping also evaluates with one or three models.

ship_thin.routing: official agents if present, else CLI

ship_detection_routing.when: (a) fails with adequate evidence (setup failure rate above 10% in any model/arm, or the CLI fidelity gates fail)
ship_detection_routing.routing: detection routing: ask for CLI or snapshots by default

hold.claim: no automatic mapping; owner decision, detection routing is the conservative default

inconclusive.when: any required evidence is missing or unknown (unfinished model, incomplete grid, unknown setup observations, insufficient coverage)

not_measured: Every arm receives an approved plan and a seed: planning from a raw user request is NOT measured.
Auth-gated and page-object-model repositories are NOT measured: the synthetic apps have no login and no POM layer, and the guide's auth rule is only exercised as a prompt, never as a login flow.
Remote or non-loopback targets, user-visible interactive questions and sanitized-snapshot fallbacks are NOT measured (the eval is non-interactive: 'ask' becomes 'stop').
Official-agent presence detection (the router's 'ready' test) is NOT measured: A, D and E always have the agents.
shipping.limitation: Point estimates over at most three model clusters; no statistical noninferiority, equivalence or population claim, and never a quality claim.

improvement_report.purpose: Say, before any data exists, when the report may print a COST improvement sentence for the CLI product paths. Descriptive reporting only: it never feeds decision.cli_first or decision.shipping and is not a statistical test.
improvement_report.per_model: Ratio of the arms' mean value per usable cell (all cells, pipeline records), so arms with different numbers of usable cells stay comparable: x over y for tokens and seconds; quality-per-100k(x) over quality-per-100k(y) (survivors over processed tokens of the same cells) for survivors per 100k processed tokens. Cells without a complete token record (or an observed elapsed time) are counted and left out of that ratio, never zero-filled. Valid-cell counts per arm and model are printed with every ratio.
improvement_report.pooled: Unweighted mean of the per-model ratios (every model counts once); undefined when any model's ratio is undefined.
improvement_report.interval: 95% percentile interval of the model-mean ratio under task-clustered bootstrap (tasks resampled with replacement; models resampled too when more than one), pooled_analysis.cluster_bootstrap replicates and the protocol seed, stdlib only. With one model it resamples the six tasks only and is a rough description, not coverage-calibrated.
improvement_report.setup_success_rate: Printed per pair and model: CLI arms 1 - user-visible setup failure rate, official arms the share of cells whose official tools were observed. Descriptive; the hard setup gate of decision.cli_first and decision.shipping is unchanged.
improvement_report.quality_condition: An improvement sentence needs the pair's quality screen: pooled point difference >= -0.10 (CLI_QUALITY_MARGIN) on all five thin metrics in both the primary and the ITT view, with common task coverage. The margin is the existing one and is not changed here.
improvement_report.allowed_sentence_rule: A pair-and-kind sentence may say 'lower measured cost' only when ALL hold: quality condition met; at least 18 cells with the needed record per arm and model; the setup gate passed for a CLI arm of the pair; the interval upper bound is below 1.0 (tokens, seconds) or its lower bound is above 1.0 (survivors per 100k tokens). Otherwise the only allowed sentence is 'cost improvement not demonstrated' with the point estimate and the interval.

forbidden_in_stage_1: any statement that the CLI arms give better, higher or more accurate quality
any pooled claim from fewer than three models beyond this tag
dollar cost (unknown unless the evidence supplies it)

improvement_report.not_a_claim: The 1.10 token rule of decision.cli_first only requires that the CLI arm is not more expensive. Only this report may say it was lower, and only under the rule above.

power_simulation.design: 1, 2 or 3 models x 6 tasks x 4 repetitions per arm; binary outcome; shared normal task/model logit intercept SD 0.60/0.35; marginal probability numerically calibrated; arms independently sampled conditional on intercepts; outcome-blind per-arm fidelity dropout. Default arms A, D, E, F, G (120 cells per model); the simulated marginal two-arm grid applies separately to each contrast, not a joint multi-arm model.
power_simulation.descriptive_trigger: For each D-A, E-D, E-B, C-E, F-A, F-D, F-E, G-F, G-E and G-A marginal contrast (E-B only when B is scheduled; C-E cross-campaign by default), pooled point gain >=.10; 80% descriptive grid MDE, not test power. Also report one-metric P(rival-minus-E estimate <=.10) at rival advantages on the same grid. The F-D and F-A contrasts reuse the same grid: a pooled F-minus-comparator estimate >= -.10 is the quality half of the CLI-first adoption rule, and the grid shows how rarely it can separate a true loss of .10 from none.
power_simulation.offline_result: Reported at baseline .7 and full fidelity, trigger probabilities at true gains 0/.05/.10/.15/.20 and the one-metric chance that a rival's advantage over E is within the .10 margin at true rival advantages 0/.10/.20. Three models (identical to the earlier artifact): .0715/.222/.4705/.762/.918 and .9285/.5295/.082. Two models (stage-1 default): .139/.2925/.522/.748/.9015 and .861/.478/.0985. One model: .2165/.331/.4935/.6425/.8085 and .7835/.5065/.1915. The descriptive 80% grid MDE is .20 for two and three models at baselines .5 and .7 and unattainable at .9; for one model it is .25 except .20 at baseline .7 with full fidelity. Monte Carlo SE <=.0112. Fewer clusters raise the chance-trigger rate under no true gain (.0715, .139, .2165 for three, two, one model), so a stage-1 point gain of .10 is weak evidence on its own. Shared-arm dependence, B/A artifact reuse, joint metrics/views, the cross-campaign C reference's time gap and costs are not simulated.
power_simulation.reason: Exact sign flips at alpha .05 have zero power for every effect with one to three model clusters (minimum p 1, .5, .25). No finite inferential MDE and no formal noninferiority power claim. The 0.10 practical margin is smaller than the 0.20 descriptive MDE. A tie is not evidence of equivalence; simulations do not model the joint sufficiency rule, outcome-dependent fidelity or unknown cost variance.
power_simulation.shipping_deficit_note: The shipping mapping's 0.20 deficit trigger equals the descriptive 80% grid MDE: a pooled deficit of 0.20 is the smallest loss the grid can separate from none about 80% of the time at two or three models and baselines .5/.7, and the one-metric chance of crossing it by chance under no true loss is the null trigger rate of the same grid. It is a point screen, not a test.

build_constraints: Offline build only: no models, containers, servers, process/port changes, network, dependency installation or freeze. Existing frozen and campaign files remain untouched.
release_gate: Owner reviews the arm set, the stage-1 roster or override, the arm C reference mode, margin/cost threshold, remaining inherited Git-environment risk, the weekly-limit plan and live validation before freezing. Account availability, read-only mount enforcement, child instruction receipt, the split-port MCP environment, sessions/token accounting need fresh live checks, the CLI exploration path (the guide's separate-port app start, the origin-allowlist guard, `--browser chromium`, the absence of the MCP declaration and of any spawned child), the CLI-first adoption rule, the shipping mapping, the setup-failure gate and the canary wiring need fresh live checks. The owner must also confirm the CLI guide against the SHIPPED router section 3 before freeze. The freeze negatively binds the whole v1 skills tree, so the campaign checkout MUST stay at the v3 skills tree until `summary` has run; 3.0.0 (the new router SKILL.md) is developed and lands in a different worktree, and the freeze takes it only as the --shipped-skill digest pin, never from the checkout's skills tree. Release checklist, shipped-skill re-pin: whenever the router SKILL.md changes after these pins (the 3.0.0 SKILL.md currently matches them byte for byte), (1) re-confirm the CLI guide against the new section 3 and edit it if the rules differ, (2) replace the vendored copy shipped-skill/SKILL.md with the new bytes and update cli_guide.estimand.shipped_skill.skill_md_sha256, skill_md_bytes and section_3_sha256 (and draft_section_3_sha256), (3) run the thin tests (they compare the 3.0.0 worktree's file with the pins) and (4) pass the final file as --shipped-skill at freeze; freeze refuses a mismatch.

Reject source/staged symlinks and added or missing staged files. Mode 0444, nested read-only directory mount. Bind the manifest in protocol and freeze; compare exact pre/post attempt manifests. Never stage reviewer SKILL.md, references, evals or agents.
scanner_gate.delta: E equals D in task, config, official agent, initialization, argv and prompt except one additional read-only scanner mount, scanner runtime staging and exactly one newline plus prompt_line. No extra model call; fixes remain in the original generating child through generator_write_test. G equals F in the same way: one additional read-only scanner mount and the scanner prompt step, nothing else.
scanner_gate.fidelity: Report scanner_gate_indicator for exact command occurrences in completed parent shell calls or root-linked persisted descendant shell calls with returned outputs. Reject explicit/duplicate identity conflicts, unlinked descendants, messages and unreturned requests. Require it for E and G as-treated and development sufficiency, separately from official-tool fidelity. This records a command attempt, not successful execution, semantic compliance or proof of fixing findings. Missing sessions can leave child execution unobserved; live-audit the sequence, findings and fixes.
scanner_gate.scanner_version: Current repository scanner bytes pinned above, the same scripts B receives. The inherited v8 scoring scanner is unchanged and distinct. Scanner is deterministic, but interpretation/fixes and shell output consume model tokens. Existing optional tool tiers may be unavailable or need downloads; record coverage in live checks, never assume a clean exit proves every tier ran.
scanner_gate.motivation: Independent finished-run analysis reports roughly 25-28k cold-start reviewer skill/reference tokens per pass (about 56% of reviewer tokens); the reviewer accounts for about 58-59% of generation+review dollars on Claude in that analysis. These reported observations motivate the hypothesis and are not new campaign measurements or model-general pricing. The deterministic scanner itself uses no model tokens.

F3_shared_server_state.problem: In v3 the generation config sets reuseExistingServer true so the parent's single test run can start while the MCP session holds the app server; the child's browser exploration had mutated that server, so the run reused polluted state. 4 of 9 mid-run arm-A cells (all three v2-23 and one v2-06) self-reported a failing generation-time run (account already deleted, tags already existed).
F3_shared_server_state.fix: Split ports by role. The staged generation config reads one environment variable, GEN_EXPLORE_PORT, which only the MCP server process receives (one extra -c mcp_servers.playwright-test.env entry). The MCP session explores on port P+10000 and may reuse its own server across setup calls; every shell command, including the parent's single test run and any child test run, has no such variable and uses the default port P with reuseExistingServer false, so it starts a fresh app process and cannot attach to the explored one. The app source gets the same variable for its listen port. A server the model starts itself on P makes the test run fail loudly (port already used) instead of silently reusing state. For F and G the same staged generation config applies, but the CLI guide has NO port instruction (it is the shipped router text): the model starts webServer.command exactly as written, which listens on the default port P (the configured baseURL), explores, and stops the app in step 6; its single shell test run then uses the same default port P with reuseExistingServer false and starts a fresh app. F and G exploration and test run are therefore sequential on port P, not on separate ports; fresh state depends on the model stopping the app, and a leftover app makes the test run fail loudly (port already used) instead of silently reusing state. The P+10000 split exists only for the MCP arms.
F3_shared_server_state.scoring_unchanged: Scoring still stages through the unmodified engine stage with the frozen configs (reuseExistingServer false, no variable); scoring_guard runs before and after scoring and checks the case configs. The split config is generation only and the deliverable is only tests/.
F3_shared_server_state.records: Each A/D/E cell records generation_config.server_isolation split-ports, the explore offset, both roles' reuse values and port-normalized config and app digests; analysis refuses mixed or mislabeled isolation per case.
F3_shared_server_state.not_proven_live: Whether the MCP server process honors the per-server env entry, whether repeated generator_setup_page calls reuse the explored server, and that the app listens on the explore port are unverified until a live smoke; the offline test proves the staged files, argv and role resolution only. For F and G it is unverified that the model stops the app it started (step 6) before its test run; a leftover app makes the test run fail loudly (port already used).

F5_scoped_writes.problem: .playwright-mcp/page-*.yml snapshots were recorded as out-of-scope writes in 6 of 9 mid-run arm-A cells, and the node_modules link replaced inside the container showed as a modified tracked file that cost the agent investigation commands.
F5_scoped_writes.fix: .git/info/exclude (written before the baseline commit) lists node_modules and .playwright-mcp/, so neither is tracked nor listed by git status. The collector lists .playwright-mcp/ files from disk into mcp_artifact_writes and keeps them out of out_of_scope_writes; they still count as secondary fidelity evidence exactly as before. The link restore after the call is unchanged. Arms F and G use the sibling .playwright-cli/ exclusion and the cli_artifact_writes listing (the CLI writes session state and snapshots under the project directory).
F5_scoped_writes.side_effect: A model command such as git clean -x would also remove ignored paths; the v3 tracked link did not have that exposure. Treated as rare and visible in transcripts.

After an independent critique: (1) arm F runs the shipped router text (section 3), so the CLI guide is semantically equal to it. cli_guide.fidelity: No official-tool class. Class cli-observed: the untruncated root command stream shows, in ONE named session and in command order, a verified `open`, a verified guard probe (`eval` of a fetch to http://127.0.0.1:9/) followed by a verified `requests` whose output shows net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT for that origin (guard_verified, required), a verified `goto` of the cell's baseURL string verbatim (when the staged baseURL is recorded; localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different origins; otherwise any loopback http origin other than the refused port 9, with goto_verbatim_checked false) and then a verified `snapshot`. A call is verified only when its executable is the Playwright CLI at a command position of the tokenized shell command (a quoted echo/grep/cat/printf argument that merely mentions the CLI is nothing; --help, -h and help are not invocations), its exit code is 0 (an unknown exit code is unverified), the shell does not mask the code (`|| true`, `|| :`, `; echo ...`, a pipe or a background `&` after the call; only a last call or one followed solely by `&&` keeps the meaning) and the returned output has no CLI error banner. The inline config shape (isolated, outputDir, a single allowed origin equal to baseURL) is reported best-effort as evidence.config_shape and gates nothing; the containment is model-enforced and the guard-verified flag is the offline check that the probe was blocked. unverified: delivered without that proof. blocked: not delivered. aborted: infrastructure outcome. The class never encodes exploration depth; browser-interaction counts (acting: goto, click, fill, press, select, eval, reload...; observing: snapshot, console...; session: open, close, requests; failed commands; guard-probe evals; zero-exploration flag) are recorded beside it. Child agents are counted per cell and arm F/G declare none.

documented_adaptations: Router step 7 (write one spec per screen under thin-rules and the project's style) is carried by the prompt line and the staged thin rules, not by the guide.
Router 'ask' branches (unknown baseURL, unnamed target, login-gated page, no CLI) become 'stop' because the eval is non-interactive; the prompt's stop clause is partial_or_blocked.

Router section 1 target rules for remote targets and production are not exercised (synthetic loopback apps); the router's sections 2, 4, 5 and 6 are not part of F's estimand except that the scanner step of section 5 is arm G's added step.
Router 'No webServer: ask the user to start the app' becomes 'stop and say so' (non-interactive).
Router 'show the webServer.command first if it is not the plain dev script' is dropped: the eval has no user to show it to; the synthetic apps' command is `node app.mjs`.

The scanner steps of arms E and G (the thin prompt lines) omit parts of the shipped section 5 gate: the 'at most 3 passes' cap on fixing P0 and P1 findings, the per-file scan with the pinned E2E_SMELL_ invocation and its exit-code rule, the BLOCKED outcome, the effective-baseURL confirmation, the refusal when the app's API/database/env points at a shared, production or private host, and the reset check before rerunning writing specs. They are NOT added to E/G because E's wording is frozen with D/E v1 and G must differ from F only by E's step; they are documented comparability differences between the E/G arms and the shipped router.

Router v4 step 1 says 'start the APPROVED webServer.command'. The benchmark task frame supplies that approval: the F/G prompt line states that the project's webServer.command and test command, run exactly as written, are approved (the user's approval of the exact commands, given once for the whole run). The router's 'show the exact command lines and get one yes' is therefore satisfied by the frame, not exercised as an interaction.

Router v4 adds safety gates that the benchmark arms do NOT exercise: the repository-is-untrusted rule with the show-and-confirm step, the loopback definition (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1; refuse origins with credentials or fragments), and the remote-target pin. The synthetic apps are trusted loopback apps with a frame-supplied approval, so these gates' effect on success or on setup failures is NOT measured.

F/G projects still carry the official agent definitions: the shared v1 project setup (frozen, used by every arm) initialises them, and skipping it for the CLI arms would mean editing frozen code. F/G models are only INSTRUCTED not to use them ('do not spawn agents and do not use the planner, generator or healer agents'); a spawn is detected by the per-cell child-agent count and blocks the F/G decision, so a violation is visible rather than assumed away. This is a comparability difference from a user project without agents.
comparability_differences: Port handling is a harness matter, not guide text. F and G explore and test sequentially on the configured default port P: the model starts webServer.command as written, stops it in step 6, and its single test run (reuseExistingServer false) starts a fresh app. The MCP arms keep the P+10000 exploration port through the GEN_EXPLORE_PORT hook, which F and G do not use. No guide text or prompt line mentions a port. This differs from the MCP arms' port separation and is a comparability difference between F/G and A/D/E.

If a synthetic app still collides on its configured port, the remedy is a harness config change, stated here as a comparability difference between the benchmark and a user project; never a guide edit.

canary.selection: The first two distinct tasks of repetition 1 of the seeded task order of the campaign schedule (outcome-blind: derived only from the seed and the task list), each for three repetitions, arm F only.
canary.order: Run and judged BEFORE the full stage. The full stage starts only after a canary verdict of proceed.
canary.stop_rule: ANY anomaly stops: archive the canary output as invalid, fix the cause, and restart as a NEW protocol version (new id, new freeze). A frozen campaign is never patched and a stopped canary is never resumed or partially counted.
anomalies: guard not verified in the observed session
child agent or unknown child count
thin rules or CLI guide not read
staged rules or guide integrity missing or changed
the six cells are not exactly the pre-registered grid
canary.implementation: Subcommand `canary --output OUT --allow-live`, run AFTER freeze, harness-check and preflight and BEFORE drive. It validates the same freeze, takes the same machine-wide lock as drive, requires the passing harness check and every roster entry decision, checks the disk floor before creating anything, and runs the six canary rows (canary_rows: the pre-registered F cells in outcome-blind order) of each ADMITTED model through the same run_model path into its own archived, non-data directory OUT/_canary/<model>/ (CANARY.json marks it; entries, the harness check and the freeze stay at OUT). It then evaluates canary_verdict (13 anomaly types plus a grid check) from transcripts and rollouts (no browser scoring), writes verdict.json, and prints PROCEED (exit 0) or STOP (exit 3); `drive` then refuses to start without a matching proceed verdict (drive_gate). A model whose run raises (usage limit, three infrastructure errors, drift) counts as an anomaly. The first stopped model stops the stage; later models are recorded as not run. STOP writes INVALID.json and prints the instruction: archive the canary directory untouched, fix the cause, restart as a NEW protocol version (new id, new freeze, new canary); do not patch the frozen campaign and do not start the full stage. The directory must not already exist: a canary is never resumed. Floors: the disk floor (minimum_free_disk_bytes) is checked before the canary and again before every cell by the inherited run_model, and the inherited load pause applies; the inherited harness has NO free-memory floor (memory is capped by the container's 4g limit), and none is added here.
canary.per_model: The canary is declared and run PER ROSTER MODEL (6 cells for each frozen model, before that model's full-stage cells); a stopped canary of any model stops the whole stage.
canary.spend: Canary cells are EXTRA spend (6 F cells per model, in budget.canary and the plan's rolls_up .. with_canary fields). They are archived as non-data and never counted in the grid: the full grid still has 24 cells per arm per model, and the same six F (task, repetition) cells run again inside it.
canary.sequence: freeze -> harness-check -> preflight (entry) -> canary -> (PROCEED) -> drive -> score -> analyze -> summary
canary.status_live: The wiring is unit-tested with stubs only; it has never run against a model.
canary.drive_gate: `drive` fails closed: before any cell it requires OUT/_canary/verdict.json with verdict proceed, bound to this freeze_sha256 (verdict.json and CANARY.json), covering exactly the admitted models, and no OUT/_canary/INVALID.json. Conversely `canary` refuses when any OUT/<model>/final.json exists (the full grid already started) or when OUT/_canary exists.
